title: Modelling Feasible Network Configurations for UMTS
contribution: A MIP model of feasible UMTS radio-network configurations over traffic snapshots (binary site, installation and assignment choices, powers switched on by binaries, SIR ratio rows with a binary right-hand side, a code-capacity knapsack from Kraft's inequality, a phantom-power approximation of soft hand-over) with linear cost and performance terms for scoring and no computations; read as ZIB-Report 02-16, the TR version, under the author name Tobias Pfender (pp. 1-2, 13-22).
problem_entry: EU project MOMENTUM (Deliverable 4.2): plan UMTS base-station sites and configurations; no single quality measure, so the model rates, costs and scores configurations; the stochastic IP is declared intractable on a personal communication, so a snapshot MIP serves as a fast surrogate of a static simulator, inside a loop that adds the snapshots a configuration fails on in simulation (pp. 2-6, 25).
key_idea: Feasibility as the feasible set of a MIP and rating as a separate weighted linear objective; linearity decides what is modelled (largest SIR ratio rather than a sum, linear objective, soft hand-over through candidate sets and a phantom power), each loss stated where it arises (pp. 13, 17-22).
assumptions: Binaries s, z, w, x and continuous powers (pp. 14-19, 27); per-snapshot blocks linked by site, installation and pilot-power variables (my reading, pp. 14-16, 27); candidate installations with precomputed attenuations, all combinations at a site assumed compatible (pp. 10, 12); semi-continuous powers (6), (8), (9) (pp. 15-16); SIR rows of the form ratio >= mu x_mi whose linear form needs a big-M the report does not give (my reading, pp. 2, 13, 15-16); perfect power control, one serving cell, no code fragmentation, fading or secondary-tree orthogonality loss (pp. 11-17); no instances or sizes; NP-hardness by citation (p. 9).
proof_devices: n/a (no algorithm, no proofs); the formulation devices follow
Kraft's inequality for prefix-free code patterns, rescaled by 2^nmax to integer coefficients, as the code-capacity knapsack row (5) (pp. 11, 15)
redundant linking row x_mi <= z_i (3) kept and footnoted as redundant given (5); (5) does not imply it in the LP relaxation, e.g. z_i = 1/2, x_mi = 1, lambda_m <= Lambda_i/2 (my check) (p. 15)
semi-continuous powers through binary on/off bounds (6), (8), (9) (pp. 15-16)
candidate sets K_mi(delta) from an attenuation-ratio threshold, delta typically 2 to 4 (3-6 dB) (p. 18)

phantom power v with 0 <= v <= rho (16) and v <= rho - rho x_mi + sum of gains of open candidate servers (17): the variable's own bound is the big-M, and rho = 0 gives back the basic uplink row (my reading) (p. 19)
minimum powers (perfect power control) left to the objective's headroom terms, not to the constraints (my reading, pp. 15, 21)
experiments: none: no instances, runs, solvers or tables; experiments promised for the soft hand-over extension (p. 20) and extensive testing on MOMENTUM real-world instances for both next research lines (p. 22); validation design only: a simulator check that adds the failing snapshots (p. 6).
positioning: Prior methods described by the WCDMA constraints they leave out (SIR target, interference, power control, soft capacity), with Amaldi et al. given the longest account (pp. 6-8); handbooks hold the data but no models (p. 6); the GSM separability of coverage and capacity is lost in UMTS (p. 9); intractability rests on a personal communication and NP-hardness on a simpler problem's result (pp. 5, 9, 25).
writing: Problem first: decisions as questions, parameters before the model, each row in words before its formula, Notice paragraphs and a footnote at the rows a simplification affects, an appendix of all parameters and variables; dense hedging; the contribution sentence opens with its limit (no detailed objective); typos left in (pp. 3, 10-17, 22, 26-27).
limits_future: Model only: objective left as proposals, soft hand-over admitted incomplete, no computation (pp. 20-22); limits stated at the point of use; next: heuristic simplification measured against the full model, or methods tailored to it, both tested on MOMENTUM real-world instances (p. 22).

method_links.note: Reverse order: a model published as a project deliverable before any instance, run or harness exists, computation promised for later; co-signed group work in another genre, before SCIP, so no counter-example to his solver practice (inferred).

Import from information theory mapped object by object (code generation patterns as prefix codes, Kraft's inequality as knapsack row (5)) after weeks of discussion with practitioners; no test decides, and the importer is not named.
Weak: the soft hand-over extension contains the basic uplink row as the setting rho = 0 (my reading of (7'), (16)); the report neither says so nor sweeps.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: full model first as the yardstick for simplifications
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The complete model is built from weeks of expert discussion before any solver can take it; the stated benefit is that the compromises of a later simplified model can be assessed precisely against it, unlike a simplified model used from the start.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: sampled scenarios with a simulator in the loop
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: The intractable stochastic IP is replaced by a MIP over traffic snapshots; the configuration is analysed in a static simulator, the snapshots it fails on are added and the optimisation restarts, or the planner relaxes the constraints.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: MIP-redundant is not LP-redundant: label the row, keep the disaggregated link
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: x_mi <= z_i (3) is footnoted as redundant given the capacity row (5) but kept; (5) does not imply it in the LP relaxation (my check). Later co-signed work: removing MIP-redundant rows can hurt by weakening the LP relaxation (R021 p. 27); omitting seemingly useful redundant information can sometimes speed up solving (R011 p. 2). Heuristic 6 context.

transferable: (D1) Replace an intractable stochastic planning problem by a MIP over sampled scenarios; check each solution in an external simulator and add the scenarios it fails on (pp. 5-6).
(D3) Discretise continuous design choices (tilt, height, direction) into candidate configurations with precomputed coefficients, and state the compatibility assumption this makes (pp. 10, 12).
(D4) Model a prefix-free code resource with Kraft's inequality, scaled by 2^nmax to integer coefficients, as a knapsack row against a budget (pp. 11, 15).
(D4) Use a conditional variable's own upper bound as the big-M of its conditional row, so that the off case follows from a bound already in the model (p. 19, rows (16)-(17)).
(D4) Keep a disaggregated linking row x <= z beside an aggregated capacity row, label it as MIP-redundant, and test it on the LP relaxation, not only on integer points (p. 15; my check).
(D4) Sparsify conditional terms with candidate sets built from a physical ratio threshold (p. 18, row (15)).

(D7) In a model paper, state each constraint in words before its formula, put each simplification in a Notice at the constraint it affects, and add an appendix with every parameter's domain and every variable's type (pp. 14-17, 26-27).
(D8) Write the complete model first, even when no solver can take it yet, so that each later simplification can be measured against it (p. 22).
